title: Rav Sama

paragraphs: [Menachot 42a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.42a.9-10) relates that Ravina and Rav Sama were sitting before Rav Ashi. Rav Sama saw that the corner of Ravina’s cloak was frayed … he said to Ravina, “Does the Master not hold…?” He [Ravina] replied, “It was said of the time of making.” Rav Sama was embarrassed. Rav Ashi said to him: “Do not be distressed; one of them is like two of us” (and Ravina was from the Land of Israel — Rashi). Hyman strongly endorses the Gaon’s proposal in Isaac Halevy’s Dorot ha-Rishonim, part 2, that the reading should be Rav Abba and Rav Sama son of Rava, and he identifies this Rav Abba as indeed a native of the Land of Israel, as explained in his entry.[^1][^2]
He is mentioned in [Bava Metzia 10b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.10b.11-14) after Ravina.

notes.text: The [printed notice](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/ba/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._III._1910.pdf#page=132) cites Halevy with the abbreviation בעדה״ר and p. 474, where the supplied Hebrew has בעדה״ד. The discussion is in Dorot ha-Rishonim, part 2, [p. 574](https://www.google.com/books/edition/_/dDgtAAAAYAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&pg=PA574) and [p. 575](https://www.google.com/books/edition/_/dDgtAAAAYAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&pg=PA575). Halevy gives Sama son of Rava parenthetically and proposes Rabbi Abba in place of Ravina, both in the Gemara and in Rashi. The consulted Gemara and [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Menachot.42a.10.3) name Ravina.
Hyman prints Bava Metzia 10a. The passage naming Rav Sama is on 10b in Davidson.
